goal: Turn these messy lecture notes into a 3-step exam study checklist
text: Cognitive Load Theory (Sweller, 1988) distinguishes intrinsic load (task complexity), extraneous load (poor formatting, dense walls of text, unclear instructions), and germane load (schema construction). When working memory capacity is exceeded by extraneous friction, executive function stalls. Bionic anchoring, progressive disclosure, and concrete action checklists reduce extraneous load so learners can focus on meaning and immediate next steps.
